thread:
alex: proposing a lightweight telemetry schema for KV/prefix cache so we can attribute hit/evict/mem signals to routes + kernel/batching choices. want quick feedback before i wire collectors.

alex: TL;DR: add three families + labels: `redwood_kv_hits_total{route,shard,tenant,kernel}` `redwood_kv_evictions_total{route,shard,tenant,evict_reason}` `redwood_kv_memory_bytes{shard,tenant,route}`. keep cardinality low for shard/tenant but allow route label for top routes only.

mina: +1 on families. couple q's: how do we pick which routes get `route` label? full cardinality would blow prometheus.

alex: plan is to surface route label only for routes in the per-tenant top-K routes table (configurable, default K=50). non-top routes map to `route="_other"`. avoids cardinality explosion.

jordan: how will this link to token-level latency breakdowns? we want to see if cache hits reduce kernel selection freq or change batch sizes.

alex: good point. propose adding `redwood_kv_hit_latency_p50` and p95 histos? maybe better: add an attribute to token latency spans: `kv_hit=true|false` and `kv_route` for sampled traces. metrics -> traces correlation for root cause.

sam: can we also include `kernel` selection distribution metric? e.g., `redwood_kernel_selected_total{kernel,route,model}` so we can see if cache hits bias choosing quantized kernels vs fp32.

alex: yup, `redwood_kernel_selected_total{kernel,route}` is in scope. but again route cardinality guarded by top-K. also add `batch_size_histogram{route}` to see batching heuristics per-route.

mina: example PromQLs would help the dashboard folks. can you add a few quick queries?

alex: sure. draft queries: 
- KV hit rate (global): `sum(rate(redwood_kv_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_kv_hits_total[5m]) + rate(redwood_kv_evictions_total[5m]))`
- Per-route hit rate (top routes): `sum by (route)(rate(redwood_kv_hits_total{route!="_other"}[5m])) / sum by (route)(rate(redwood_kv_hits_total{route!="_other"}[5m]) + rate(redwood_kv_evictions_total{route!="_other"}[5m]))`
- Memory footprint per-tenant: `sum by (tenant)(redwood_kv_memory_bytes)`
- Kernel selection skew when cache hit vs miss: `sum by (kernel) (rate(redwood_kernel_selected_total{kv_hit="true"}[5m])) / sum by (kernel) (rate(redwood_kernel_selected_total[5m]))`

jordan: nice. for the dashboard panels: want a per-route small multiples view with columns: hit rate, evictions/min, mean batch size, median token latency. panels should allow toggling by tenant.

sam: ops concern -> eviction_reason label might be high cardinality. use coarse reasons: `memory_pressure`, `ttl`, `manual_invalidate`, `shard_rebalance`.

alex: agreed. keep evict_reason set to those four. also we should emit `redwood_kv_reuse_routes_total{route,origin_route}` to capture reuse where one route benefits from prefix share with another. that helps identify cross-route temporal locality.

mina: reuse_routes metric is great for attribution but origin_route can explode. again top-K policy? maybe only emit when origin route is also in top-K, otherwise `_other`.

alex: yep. clarify in schema: origin_route label only populated if both sides in top-K, else `_other`.

infra-bot: deploy check: datasource changes detected -> adding 7 metric series, estimated scrape cardinality +10k series worst-case. review required by eng-infra.

sam: perf/regression detection idea: add alerts: 
- kv_hit_rate_drop: when per-tenant hit rate drops > 15% vs 1h baseline for 10m
- kv_memory_bloat: when tenant memory increases > 30% in 15m
- kernel_shift_alert: sudden >40% change in kernel selection distribution over 5m

jordan: also add dashboard panel showing `token_latency` split by `kv_hit` label P50/P95 to confirm impact.

alex: implementation notes for collectors: 
- emit counters on every hit/evict/select with low-overhead atomic ops.
- sample batch_size as a separate histogram on batch commit events.
- memory_bytes emitted periodically from shard owner every 10s to avoid bursts.
- tracing: add `kv_hit` boolean tag to token generation spans for sampled traces.

alex: small example of metric exposition snippet (go):
```go
kvHits.WithLabelValues(routeLabel, shardID, tenantID, kernelName).Inc()
kvMemGauge.WithLabelValues(shardID, tenantID, routeLabel).Set(float64(bytes))
```

mina: can we gate route label emission behind a feature flag so we can rollout?

alex: yes, rollout via config: `telemetry.top_k_routes_per_tenant` and `telemetry.emit_route_labels=true|false`. default: emit=false for 1st rollout, flip to true after infra checks.

sam: timeline? checkbox: schema PR -> infra review -> flagged rollout -> dashboards -> alerts. we should aim to land schema PR in 2 weeks.

alex: planning PR today. tagging eng-infra and observability for review. requests: @mina please draft dashboard panels (use my queries), @jordan please add token-latency trace tag instrumentation, @sam please coordinate alert definitions with oncall.

mina: got it, will prototype 3 panels and share screenshots in this thread next week.

jordan: will add trace tag + kernel metric in my change.

sam: will draft alerts and ping infra.

alex: thanks all. small followup: do we want `route` to be service route or customer-facing path? leaning toward logical route id (the canonical route we use in routing table) not raw URL. avoids PII and noisy variants.

mina: agree, logical route id is better.

sam: thumbs up. :thumbsup:

alex: will open PR and link here.
